User story: As an admin, I want my query split into words regardless of case and extra spaces so that 'GET  mguser' and 'get mguser' find the same cmdlets.
Expected behaviour: queryTokens lower-cases the query, splits on any run of whitespace and drops empty pieces (sources.ts:34). Names are compared against lower-cased copies (search.worker.ts:42). Leading/trailing/multiple spaces produce no extra tokens; a whitespace-only query yields zero tokens and behaves like an empty query. The same tokeniser drives result-name highlighting (ResultList.tsx:155-170), so each matched token that appears literally in the name is wrapped in <mark>.
How to test: Type 'GET-MGUSER' then '  get-mguser  ' into the search input; result count and order are identical and the first row is Get-MgUser with 'get-mguser' highlighted in a <mark>. Type '   ' and confirm the full list (same count as empty query) is shown.
Test result: Ran Playwright against :4400 at 1440x900 and 390x844, dark and light. 'GET-MGUSER' and '  get-mguser  ' both give 5,339 results with the same order; the first row is Get-MgUser with <mark>Get-MgUser</mark>. 'get   mguser' gives 2,287 with both tokens marked. Mark contrast is fine in both themes and nothing overflows at 390. Whitespace-only '   ' gives 40,931 rows like an empty query, but the label reads '40,931 results · 13 ms' and the URL becomes /?q=+++.
Errors found:
SRCH-01.E1 [logic/low] A whitespace-only query does not behave like an empty query. The tokens are empty, so the rows are right, but the count label still shows the '· N ms' timing because App.tsx tests results.q (the raw string) rather than the tokens. The URL is written as ?q=+++, so the blank query also survives reloads and shared links. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400, wait for the results, then type three spaces into the search box. Observed: '40,931 results · 13 ms' and the URL is /?q=+++. Expected: '40,931 results' with no timing and no q parameter, the same as an empty box.
SRCH-01.E2 [ux/low] Highlighting drops overlapping tokens by start position only. When a short token and a longer token start at the same spot, the short one wins and the longer, more relevant match is not highlighted. REPRO: Search 'get get-mguser'. Observed: the first row Get-MgUser highlights only 'Get'. Expected: the whole 'Get-MgUser' (the exact match) highlighted.

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet whose name I typed exactly to appear at the top so that I can open it immediately.
Expected behaviour: A token equal to the full lower-cased name scores 1000, the highest per-token score (search.worker.ts:102). Results are sorted by total score descending (search.worker.ts:163), so an exact match outranks any prefix match of the same token.
How to test: Search 'get-mguser' in the Graph scope; first row is Get-MgUser, ahead of Get-MgUserMessage etc.
Test result: Clicked the Graph scope and searched 'get-mguser'. The first rows are Get-MgUser, Get-MgUserById and Get-MgUserChat (5,337 results). A Node re-implementation of scoreToken over the dist index matches the UI order exactly: exact 1000, then prefixes at 796.

User story: As an admin, I want names that start with what I typed ranked highly, with the closest-length name first, so that partial typing quickly lands on the right cmdlet.
Expected behaviour: If the name starts with the token, score = 800 - min(100, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:103): shorter names that start with the token rank higher, and the penalty caps at 100 so any prefix match (>=700) beats a noun-prefix of equal length difference and every substring match. Ties are broken by shorter name length, then by ref (source order in SOURCES, then index order) (search.worker.ts:163).
How to test: Search 'get-mgus'; rows start with Get-MgUser and continue with longer Get-MgUser* names in increasing length; no row whose name merely contains 'get-mgus' later in the name appears above a prefix row.
Test result: Searched 'get-mgus': 7,473 results. In the simulation, the first 573 rows are all prefix matches with name length never decreasing. No prefix row appears after row 573; the first non-prefix row is Get-MgBetaUser (fuzzy). The UI shows the same top 12 rows.

User story: As an admin, I want to type just the noun (e.g. 'mailbox') and see cmdlets whose noun starts with it so that I can find all verbs for an object without knowing the verb.
Expected behaviour: The noun is the lower-cased name after the first hyphen, only when the hyphen is not at position 0; names without a hyphen have an empty noun (search.worker.ts:51). If the noun starts with the token, score = 700 - min(100, nounLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:104-105). Name-prefix matches take precedence over noun-prefix (checked first).
How to test: Search 'mailbox' in Exchange scope; top rows are Get-Mailbox, Set-Mailbox, New-Mailbox, etc. (noun exactly 'mailbox'), followed by longer nouns like MailboxPermission.
Test result: In the Exchange scope, searching 'mailbox' gives Get, New, Set, Enable, Remove, Search, Connect, Disable and Restore-Mailbox (all noun 700). Get-MailboxPlan and the other longer nouns follow. All scope behaves the same (718 results).

Feature: Substring match anywhere in the name
User story: As an admin, I want a word found inside a cmdlet name to match even if it is not at the start of the verb or noun so that I can find cmdlets by any part of their name.
Expected behaviour: If the token occurs anywhere in the lower-cased name, score = 520 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:106-107): earlier occurrences rank higher, floor 400. Always below prefix and noun-prefix matches.
How to test: Search 'permission'; rows like Get-MailboxPermission appear (substring in noun), ranked below any cmdlet whose noun starts with 'permission'.
Test result: Searching 'permission' (874 results): the top rows are Add-ADPermission and Get-ADPermission (substring score 514). In the simulation, no row has a noun or name starting with 'permission', so there is no higher class to outrank. Get-MailboxPermission is a substring hit at index 27 (All) and index 6 (Exchange).

User story: As an admin, I want to type 'getmguser' without the hyphen so that I can search quickly without punctuation.
Expected behaviour: Each name also has a hyphen-stripped form (search.worker.ts:14,50). The token is also stripped of hyphens; the flat comparison runs only when the token contained a hyphen or the stripped token is at least 4 chars (search.worker.ts:108-109). A hit scores 480 - min(120, position) (search.worker.ts:110-111), below a real substring match. Tokens of 1-3 chars without hyphens skip this step. A token with misplaced hyphens (e.g. 'get-mg-user') still matches via the flat form.
How to test: Search 'getmguser'; Get-MgUser is in the top results. Search 'get-mg-user'; Get-MgUser is still found.
Test result: 'getmguser' and 'get-mg-user' each give 573 results with Get-MgUser first (flat match, score 480). Hyphenless results are not highlighted (no <mark>), which is consistent with the literal-only highlighter.
Errors found: SRCH-06.E1 [ux/low] Hyphenless and misplaced-hyphen queries return a very different result set from the hyphenated form, and the matched part is not highlighted. 'getmguser' gives 573 results, while 'get-mguser' gives 5,339, mostly fuzzy noise. A user has no visual cue for why a row matched. REPRO: Search 'get-mguser', then 'getmguser'. Observed: the counts are 5,339 and 573, and no row of the second search shows any <mark>.

User story: As an admin, I want slightly misspelled queries to still find cmdlets so that a typo mid-task does not return nothing.
Expected behaviour: Only for tokens of 4+ chars and only when no exact/prefix/noun/substring/flat match applied (search.worker.ts:113). fuzzy() requires the token to be an in-order subsequence of the name, adding the current contiguous run length per char (search.worker.ts:82-97). The row matches only if the score >= 45% of the perfect score n(n+1)/2; score = 120 + round(ratio*80) - min(60, nameLength - tokenLength) (search.worker.ts:115-117), i.e. between ~60 and 200, below all literal matches. Transposed letters that break subsequence order (characters missing or reordered) return 0.
How to test: Search 'get-mgusr' (dropped letter); Get-MgUser appears in results ranked below literal matches. Search 'xyzq' and confirm it returns no fuzzy rows.
Test result: 'get-mgusr' finds Get-MgUser first (fuzzy 185); 'xyzq' gives 0. However, the simulation shows fuzzy accounts for 4,766 of the 5,339 results for 'get-mguser' and all 5,932 for 'get-mgusr'. A transposition such as 'get-mgsuer' gives 3,543 results led by Get-MgSecurityAlert and does not contain Get-MgUser. 'gte-mguser' and 'get-mg-usr' give 0.
Errors found:
SRCH-07.E1 [ux/medium] The fuzzy threshold (45% of n(n+1)/2) is very loose for long tokens. A 6-character contiguous run plus scattered letters is enough to match, so an exact or near-exact query pulls in thousands of irrelevant rows and the result count is misleading. Fuzzy junk also outranks genuine description matches. Meanwhile common typos (transposed letters) find nothing useful and show thousands of unrelated rows instead. REPRO: 1) Search 'get-mguser'. Observed: 5,339 results, about 4,766 of them fuzzy, e.g. Get-MgSiteTermStoreSetParentGroupSetTermRelationSet. 2) Search 'get-mgsuer'. Observed: 3,543 results led by Get-MgSecurityAlert, and Get-MgUser is absent. 3) Search 'retention' and scroll to the end. Observed: Get-MgBetaGroupThreadPostMentionCount (a fuzzy name match, description 'Get the number of the resource') ranks above Restore-AzSqlServer, whose description actually mentions retention. Expected: typo tolerance that finds the intended cmdlet without flooding the list. Possible fixes: a stricter threshold for long tokens, skipping fuzzy when literal hits exist, or an edit-distance approach.
SRCH-07.E2 [docs/low] The story says the fuzzy score falls 'between ~60 and 200'. The minimum possible is 120 + round(0.45*80) - 60 = 96. REPRO: Compute from search.worker.ts:117 with ratio 0.45 and a length penalty of 60.

User story: As an admin, I want words from a cmdlet's description to match when the name does not so that I can search by what a cmdlet does.
Expected behaviour: If no name-based rule matched and descriptions are loaded for the source, a token contained in the lower-cased description scores 60 (search.worker.ts:119), the lowest non-zero score, so description-only hits always sort below name matches. Before descriptions load (ldesc null) such rows do not match at all.
How to test: After the page settles, search a word that appears only in descriptions (e.g. 'retention'); rows whose names lack the word but whose description contains it appear after name matches.
Test result: Searching 'retention' gives 175 results after the page settles. The simulation puts the 7 description-only rows (score 60) last, starting at index 168, with no name match after them. The UI tail shows those rows with their description text. Delaying *desc.json with page.route gives 168 results before the descriptions load and 175 after, with row descriptions filled in.

User story: As an admin, I want every word I type to have to match so that 'user license' narrows results instead of widening them.
Expected behaviour: For each row every token is scored independently; if any token scores 0 the row is excluded (search.worker.ts:155-158). Matching rows are ranked by the sum of token scores, then shorter name, then ref (search.worker.ts:163). Tokens may match different parts (name, noun, flat, fuzzy, description).
How to test: Search 'mguser license'; every result contains both terms (e.g. Get-MgUserLicenseDetail) and none matches only one. Add a nonsense third token 'zzzz' and confirm 0 results.
Test result: 'mguser license' gives 20 results; adding 'zzzz' gives 0. Every row matches both tokens, but not always in the name. Remove-MgUser, Remove-MgUserByUserPrincipalName, Remove-MgBetaUser and others match 'license' only through their description. Get-MgReportTeamUserActivityCount matches 'mguser' only by fuzzy and 'license' only by description.
Errors found: SRCH-09.E1 [docs/low] The How-to-test step says every result contains both terms and none matches only one. In fact, rows whose names contain only 'mguser' (description-only 'license') appear, ranked above names that contain both literal 'license' and a fuzzy 'mguser'. This matches the expected-behaviour text but contradicts the test step. REPRO: Search 'mguser license'. Row 7 is Remove-MgUser (score 700 + 60), above Invoke-MgLicenseUser (156 + 511).

Feature: Empty query lists everything in index order
User story: As an admin, I want an empty search box to show all cmdlets in the current scope so that I can browse or just filter by facets.
Expected behaviour: With zero tokens every row that passes the filters gets score 1 (search.worker.ts:154) and no sort is applied (search.worker.ts:163), so results are in source order (SOURCES order) then shard index order. The result count label omits the timing ('· N ms') when q is empty (App.tsx:152).
How to test: Clear the search box with scope 'All'; result count equals the total cmdlet count in the placeholder ('Search N cmdlets') and no ' ms' timing is shown. Type a query and the '· N ms' suffix appears.
Test result: With an empty box in All scope, the count is '40,931 results' with no ms, matching the placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets'. The first row is Add-MgApplicationKey (graph index 0). At the Graph/Az boundary (row 27,327), the last Graph rows are followed by Add-AzADAppPermission. Scrolling to the bottom shows the last MECM rows, Update-CMClientStatus and Update-CMDistributionPoint, matching the index order. Typing a query adds '· N ms'. A whitespace-only query wrongly shows the timing (see SRCH-01). A 300-character unbroken no-match query makes the empty-state title overflow and clips the hint at 390px.
Errors found: SRCH-10.E1 [ux/low] The no-match empty state does not wrap long unbroken queries. The title grows to about 2,600px inside the results pane, so both the title and the hint line ('Get-MgUse…') are clipped at 390px. REPRO: At 390x844, type 300 'a' characters. Observed: .empty-title has scrollWidth 2619 and the text is cut off at the pane edge. Expected: overflow-wrap:anywhere, or truncating the echoed query.

Feature: Scope search to one source or all sources
User story: As an admin, I want to restrict searching to one product (Graph, Az, Exchange…) or search all so that results are relevant to the module I am using.
Expected behaviour: filters.source selects a Scope: 'all' covers every source, a source id covers only that source (sources.ts:53-79). The worker searches only loaded shards whose id is in the scope (search.worker.ts:148-149). Unknown or missing scope ids from the URL fall back to 'all' (sources.ts:77). Per-source scopes have placeholder 'Search N <Short> cmdlets', 'all' has 'Search N cmdlets' (sources.ts:56,68).
How to test: Open /?source=graph (or pick Graph) and search 'user'; every row is a Graph row. Open with ?source=bogus and confirm results span all sources and placeholder reads 'Search <total> cmdlets'.
Test result: /?s=graph&q=user: 8,684 results, all rows tinted with the Graph colour (#9b8cff), placeholder 'Search 27,327 Graph cmdlets'. /?s=bogus&q=get: falls back to All, 16,834 results, placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets', 'All' tab pressed, bogus param dropped from the URL. Placeholders for az/entra/exchange/mecm are correct. The test step's '?source=graph' is ignored (10,301 results across all sources).
Errors found: SRCH-11.E1 [docs/low] The story's How-to-test uses '/?source=graph', but the app's URL parameter is 's' (url.ts:15). Following the documented link silently searches every source. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400/?source=graph&q=user. Observed: placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets', 10,301 results from all sources, URL rewritten to /?q=user. Expected (per story): a Graph-only scope.

Feature: Facet filters (verb, module, category, extra, has examples)
User story: As an admin, I want to filter results by verb, module, category, API version/site role and whether examples exist so that I can narrow large result sets.
Expected behaviour: A row passes only if each non-empty filter equals the row's value exactly: verb, module, category, extra, and, when examples is true, the row must have examples (search.worker.ts:123-132). Filters are applied before scoring and combine with the query (AND).
How to test: Search 'user' in Graph, set Verb=Get; all rows start with 'Get-'. Toggle 'has examples'; count drops and every opened row shows examples. Set extra=beta; all rows carry the beta tag.
Test result: Graph 'user': 8,684 results. Verb=Get gives 4,083, all rows Get-*. Has examples gives 646. API=beta gives 360, all Get-MgBeta*. The opened row shows an Examples block. Filters combine with AND and are written to the URL (verb, ex, ver).
Errors found:
SRCH-12.E1 [ux/medium] A filter value that is not in the current facet list stays active but is invisible. The verb <select> renders blank (selectedIndex -1, neither 'Any' nor the value) and the list is empty. This happens when switching source, because setSource keeps the verb (App.tsx:111), and with stale or hand-edited links. REPRO: Open /?s=az&verb=Approve (9 results), then click the Entra tab. Observed: 0 results, 'Nothing matches these filters.', and a blank Verb select (the options are Any plus Entra verbs). The only way back is Reset or picking a verb. The same happens with /?verb=Bogus. Expected: drop or flag an unavailable verb, or show it as a selected '(not in this source)' option.
SRCH-12.E2 [ux/medium] In the All scope, module and API/extra filters from the URL still apply but have no control (the Module and extra selects are hidden for All). The Filters chip shows '1' and results narrow, but the user can't see what is filtering. REPRO: Open /?module=Az.Compute and click Filters. Observed: 292 results, chip 'Filters 1', panel shows only Verb=Any, Category=Any, Has examples and Reset. The same happens with /?ver=beta&q=user (5,258 rows, beta only). Expected: either ignore per-source filters in All, or show them.

User story: As an admin, I want the filter dropdowns to list the values available in my current scope so that I only pick options that exist.
Expected behaviour: Each results message carries facets computed from all rows of the scoped sources (not narrowed by query or other filters): de-duplicated, empties removed, sorted with localeCompare (search.worker.ts:134-143,165). Verbs and categories are always provided; modules and extras are provided only for a single-source scope and are empty arrays for 'all' (sources.ts:49-50,60,72).
How to test: With scope 'All', confirm module and extra filters are not offered (empty lists). Switch to Graph; module list and the extra (API version) list appear, alphabetically sorted. Type a query and confirm facet lists do not shrink.
Test result: All scope: the filter panel shows only Verb (99 values) and Category (sorted with localeCompare), and no Module or extra. Graph shows Verb, Module (83, localeCompare-sorted), Category, and API [beta, v1.0]. Typing 'zzzqqq' (0 results) leaves 83 modules and 54 verbs, so facets don't shrink with the query. Az and Exchange show no extra (none defined). MECM shows 'Site role' and no Module (only one module). This matches the UI's >1 rule.

Feature: Names-first loading, descriptions later with automatic re-rank
User story: As an admin, I want results as soon as the name index is loaded, with descriptions filling in afterwards, so that I can start searching without waiting for the larger description files.
Expected behaviour: The worker loads all name shards first (search.worker.ts:69) and answers searches once they are in. Only then does it fetch descriptions for every source (search.worker.ts:71-73). When they arrive it re-runs the latest search under the same id (search.worker.ts:76), so the client accepts it (it is still latest) and description-only matches are added and rows now include desc text. Rows fetched before descriptions arrive have desc '' (search.worker.ts:183). A description fetch failure for a source is swallowed and that source simply keeps name-only search (search.worker.ts:59-60). While no results have arrived the count reads 'Loading index…' (App.tsx:150-151).
How to test: Throttle network, load the page and type a description-only word; at first no description-only hits appear, then after desc files load the list refreshes with additional rows and row descriptions appear. Block a /a/<build>/idx/*desc* request and confirm name search still works with no error shown.
Test result: Held the *.desc.json requests with Playwright routing. The names-only search for 'retrieves' gave 0 results. After the desc files were released, the same search id was re-run (two results messages with the same id) and showed 209 results with descriptions in the rows. Aborting graph.desc.json gave name search 5,339 results for get-mguser, no alert, and Graph rows show the module in place of desc. A 500 on graph.desc gave 188 results for 'retrieves' (Graph desc skipped).
Errors found: SRCH-14.E1 [ux/medium] While descriptions are still loading, a description-only query shows the final-looking empty state "No match for 'retrieves'." and '0 results · N ms'. A moment later results appear. On a slow connection (graph.desc.json is 2 MB) the admin is told there's no match and may give up or rephrase. Nothing shows that descriptions are still loading. REPRO: Delay requests matching *.desc.json (devtools throttling or request blocking), then open /?q=retrieves. Observed: '0 results · 28 ms' and "No match for 'retrieves'." until the desc files load, then 209 results. Expected: a 'searching descriptions…' hint, or no definitive empty state until descriptions are in.

User story: As an admin, I want a clear message if the search index cannot load so that I know the site is broken rather than waiting forever.
Expected behaviour: If any source shard fetch fails (non-2xx throws 'HTTP <status> for <path>', sources.ts:24-27), Promise.all rejects, the worker logs '[psindex] index load failed' and posts a single 'load-error' with the message (search.worker.ts:77-80). Subsequent searches and requests are never answered (search.worker.ts:236,239-240); client request promises never settle (client.ts:125-128). The UI shows 'Index unavailable' as the count and a LoadFailed panel with the message in the results area (App.tsx:148-149,186).
How to test: Block one idx shard request (e.g. via devtools request blocking) and reload; count label reads 'Index unavailable' and the results pane shows the failure message containing 'HTTP'. Typing further produces no results and no errors.
Test result: Fulfilled exchange.json with 404: count 'Index unavailable', and a role=alert panel 'The search index didn't load. HTTP 404 for idx/exchange.json. Check your connection, then reload the page.' with a Reload button. The console logged '[psindex] index load failed'. Typing and switching tabs keep 'Index unavailable' with no errors. Abort gives 'Failed to fetch'. Bad JSON gives a SyntaxError message. Layout is fine at 390px in light and dark.
Errors found:
SRCH-15.E1 [ux/medium] A shard request that stalls (never completes or errors) leaves the page on 'Loading index…' with skeleton rows forever. No timeout is applied, so the admin waits indefinitely, which is the case this story exists to prevent. REPRO: Route **/idx/mecm.json and never respond (or simulate a hung connection), then open /. After 8 s and later: count reads 'Loading index…', skeleton rows show, and no error appears. Expected: after a reasonable timeout, show LoadFailed.
SRCH-15.E2 [ux/low] The error copy always says 'Check your connection'. For a 404 or a malformed JSON shard the problem is on the server side, so the advice is misleading. The deep-linked entry (?c=...) is also silently not opened. REPRO: Fulfill mecm.json with 200 '{bad'. Observed: "Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 ... Check your connection, then reload the page."

Feature: Search ids and stale result dropping
User story: As an admin typing quickly, I want only the results for my latest keystroke shown so that the list never flickers back to an older query.
Expected behaviour: Each client.search increments a shared sequence and records it as latestSearch (client.ts:115-118). Results whose id differs from latestSearch are ignored (client.ts:109). In the worker, searches that queue behind the index load are dropped unless they are still the last one received (search.worker.ts:233-236). The description re-run reuses the latest id, so it replaces current results (search.worker.ts:74-76). Requests (rows/related/find) share the sequence and are matched to replies by id; each reply resolves once and is removed (client.ts:110,129-135). The latest id is exposed via client.latest for Enter-to-open (client.ts:121-123; App.tsx:143).
How to test: With slow network, type 'g', 'ge', 'get-mguser' rapidly before the index loads; only one result set arrives and it is for 'get-mguser' (first row Get-MgUser).
Test result: Held all name shards and typed 'get-mguser' at 30 ms/key before load (ids 1-11). The worker posted results only for id 11 (q='get-mguser'): once on load and once on the desc re-run, same id. The first row is Get-MgUser, 5,339 results. Pressing Enter before load opened Get-Mailbox once results arrived. After load, rapid typing 'set-mailbox' ended on Set-Mailbox (33 results), and a final empty query showed 40,931.
Errors found: SRCH-16.E1 [accessibility/low] The result count is an aria-live=polite region that includes the timing ('· 12 ms'). Every keystroke changes it, so screen readers re-announce count plus milliseconds on every search, which is noisy, and the timing changes even when the count doesn't. REPRO: With a screen reader, type 'get-mguser' character by character. Each result set announces e.g. '5,339 results · 30 ms'.

User story: As an admin, I want large result lists to scroll smoothly so that browsing tens of thousands of cmdlets stays fast.
Expected behaviour: Results carry only an Int32Array of refs ((sourceIndex << 20) | rowIndex), transferred without copying (search.worker.ts:6-7,25-26,164-165). The list asks the worker for 'rows' only for the visible window (ResultList.tsx:96-101); the worker decodes each ref into a full Row with key, source, name, verb, module, category, extra, file, moduleVersion, perms, examples, desc and dup (search.worker.ts:168-186,220).
How to test: Clear the query in 'All' scope and scroll quickly to the bottom; rows render (skeleton briefly) and the last rows show real names.
Test result: All scope, empty query: the scroller is 2,619,584 px (40,931 × 64). Jumping to the bottom renders real rows, and the last is Update-CMDistributionPoint, which matches the last mecm shard entry. Rapid wheel scrolling (30 × -20000) left 0 skeletons and 26 materialised rows after 600 ms.

User story: As an admin viewing a cmdlet, I want to see other verbs for the same noun so that I can jump from Get-Mailbox to Set-Mailbox.
Expected behaviour: related resolves the key (see find), then collects other rows in the same source with an identical noun, excluding the row itself, stopping at 30 rows taken in index order, then sorts them by verb with localeCompare (search.worker.ts:206-216). Names with no hyphen (empty noun) or unknown keys return []. Duplicated names in other modules with the same noun are included (only the row index is excluded).
How to test: Open Get-Mailbox in Exchange; the related list shows Set-Mailbox, New-Mailbox, Remove-Mailbox etc., alphabetical by verb, never Get-Mailbox itself, and at most 30 entries.
Test result: exchange:Get-Mailbox lists 'Same noun · Mailbox': Connect, Disable, Enable, New, Remove, Restore, Search and Set-Mailbox. The list is alphabetical by verb, excludes Get-Mailbox, and has fewer than 30 items. The duplicated noun Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy (MicrosoftTeams) includes the SkypeForBusiness duplicate with a '· module' suffix. No noun in the data exceeds 11 rows, so the 30 cap is never hit.
Errors found: SRCH-18.E1 [accessibility/low] Activating a related-cmdlet button replaces the Detail (it is keyed by row), so the focused button is removed and focus falls back to <body>. Keyboard and screen reader users lose their place and must tab from the top of the page. REPRO: Open /?c=exchange:Get-CsExternalAccessPolicy, Tab to the first related button, press Enter. Observed: document.activeElement is <body>. Expected: focus moves to the new detail heading (or stays in the pane).

Feature: Find by link key, including legacy, unqualified and duplicate names
User story: As an admin opening a shared link, I want it to resolve to the right cmdlet even if the link is old, differs in case, or the name exists in several modules so that bookmarks keep working.
Expected behaviour: Row keys are 'source:name', qualified as 'source:name@module' only when the name repeats within the source (search.worker.ts:16,32,52). parseKey splits on ':' and '@' (search.worker.ts:33-37). refOfKey finds the source by id (unknown source -> null), compares names case-insensitively, returns the row whose module matches exactly when a module is given, otherwise the first row with that name; an unqualified key or a module that no longer exists falls back to the first same-name row; no name match -> null (search.worker.ts:188-204). find returns that Row or null (search.worker.ts:222-225), and Row.dup tells the UI to show the module (types.ts:230).
How to test: Open a deep link with key 'exchange:get-mailbox' (lower case) and confirm Get-Mailbox opens. For a duplicated name (e.g. an Entra cmdlet in v1.0 and beta), open 'entra:<Name>' without @module and confirm the first one opens; open 'entra:<Name>@<beta module>' and confirm the beta row opens; open 'entra:<Name>@NoSuchModule' and confirm fallback to the first. Feature: Detail header: cmdlet name and source/module tags
User story: As an admin, I want the opened cmdlet's name, source and module shown at the top of the detail pane so that I know exactly which cmdlet and module I am reading.
Expected behaviour:
Opening a row renders
with its source colour applied via srcStyle (inline style). h2#detail-title contains {row.name}. The .tags row always shows span.tag.tag-source holding a .source-dot plus the source's short label (e.g. Graph, Az, Entra, Exchange, MECM), then span.tag with the module name.
How to test: Search for e.g. Get-MgUser, click the result. Assert #detail-title code text equals the cmdlet name; .detail .tags .tag-source text equals the source short name; the second .tag equals the module (e.g. Microsoft.Graph.Users).
Test result: Tested by searching 'Get-MgUser' and clicking the result at 1440x900, and through ?c= deep links for 12 cmdlets across all 5 sources at 1440 and 390 in both themes. article.detail[aria-labelledby=detail-title] has style '--src: #9b8cff;'. #detail-title code = Get-MgUser. The tags are tag-source 'Graph' (with .source-dot) followed by 'Microsoft.Graph.Users'. Exchange, Az, Entra and MECM short labels are correct. The markup matches the story, but the accessibility tree is wrong: the heading and article names include the copy button.
Errors found: DETL-01.E1 [accessibility/medium] The Copy name button sits inside h2#detail-title. Because the article is aria-labelledby that h2, both the heading's and the article's accessible names become 'Get-MgGroup Copy name', or 'Get-MgGroup Copied' right after a copy. A screen reader user moving by heading hears the button label as part of the cmdlet name. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400/?c=graph:Get-MgGroup and click the copy icon. Playwright ariaSnapshot of article.detail shows: article "Get-MgGroup Copied" > heading "Get-MgGroup Copied" [level=2]. Expected: heading/article name 'Get-MgGroup', with the button outside the h2 or labelled only by the code element.

User story: As an admin, I want to see a module's own version when it differs from its source's version so that I know which module release the docs describe.
Expected behaviour: A tag 'v{moduleVersion}' with title="Module version" is shown only when row.moduleVersion is non-empty AND differs from the source's version (e.g. Teams 8.1.0 under Exchange, each Az.* module). It is hidden when moduleVersion is '' or equal to the source version.
How to test: Open an Az cmdlet (e.g. Get-AzVM): assert .tags .tag[title='Module version'] exists with text starting 'v'. Open a cmdlet whose module version equals its source's version (or is unknown): assert that tag is absent.
Test result: Exchange behaves as specified: Get-CsOnlineUser and Get-Team show tag[title='Module version'] 'v8.1.0', Export-WhiteboardHtml shows 'v1.9.0', and ExchangePowerShell (3.9.2 = source) shows none. The story's own test fails: ?c=az:Get-AzVM shows only 'Az | Az.Compute | Get', with no version tag. All 213 Az entries in the shipped index have fileVersions '' because every data/az/modules/*.json has "version": null. Graph and Entra versions always equal the source version, so the tag never shows for them (correct).
Errors found: DETL-02.E1 [logic/medium] No Az cmdlet shows a module version, although the story names 'each Az.* module' as the main case. The committed Az data has version:null for all 221 module files. The pipeline's gallery_dependencies() turns a failed PowerShell Gallery lookup into a ::warning:: and {}, so the blank versions were committed and built without any check failing. REPRO: 1) Open http://localhost:4400/?c=az:Get-AzVM and check .tags: no .tag[title='Module version']. 2) python3 -c "import json,glob;print({json.load(open(f))['version'] for f in glob.glob('/home/user/psindex/data/az/modules/*.json')})" prints {None}. Expected a tag such as 'v<Az.Compute version>'.

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet's verb shown as a tag so that I can see at a glance whether it reads, creates, changes or removes.
Expected behaviour: When row.verb is non-empty a span.tag with the verb (e.g. Get, Set, New) is rendered after the module/version tags; when verb is empty no verb tag is rendered.
How to test: Open Get-MgUser; assert a .tags .tag with text 'Get' exists.
Test result: Get-MgUser shows a 'Get' tag after the module tag; Set-Mailbox shows 'Set'; Add-, Invoke- and Disconnect- also checked. The index has no empty verbs in any source, so the empty branch cannot be reached with real data (the code guards it with row.verb &&).

User story: As an admin, I want a category tag only when it adds information beyond the module name so that the header is not cluttered with repeats.
Expected behaviour: A category tag is shown only when row.category is non-empty, is not equal to row.module, and row.module does not end with '.' + category (e.g. category 'Groups' is hidden for module Microsoft.Graph.Groups).
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet in Microsoft.Graph.Groups (e.g. Get-MgGroup) and assert no .tag with text 'Groups'. Open a cmdlet whose category differs from its module and assert the category tag is present.
Test result: Get-MgGroup (Microsoft.Graph.Groups) shows no 'Groups' tag. Get-MgUser shows 'User Management'. Get-CMDevice shows 'Device Management'.
Errors found: DETL-04.E1 [ux/low] The redundancy rule only catches '<module>.<category>'. So module 'MicrosoftTeams' still gets category 'Teams', and 'WhiteboardAdmin' gets 'Whiteboard', which repeats the module name. REPRO: Open ?c=exchange:Get-Team. Tags: Exchange, MicrosoftTeams, v8.1.0, Get, Teams.

User story: As an admin, I want beta API cmdlets visibly flagged so that I do not accidentally use a beta endpoint in production.
Expected behaviour: When row.extra is non-empty a tag with the extra value (API version for Graph/Entra, site role for MECM) is shown. If the value equals the source's extra.warn ("beta" for Graph and Entra) the tag also has class tag-warn (warning colour). Other extra values (e.g. v1.0) render as a plain tag.

MECM site roles appear as plain tags ('Primary' on Add-CMBoundaryToGroup, 'SMS Provider' on Disconnect-CMTrackedObject). The logic is correct, but in the light theme the beta warning is nearly unreadable.
Errors found:
DETL-05.E1 [accessibility/high] --warn (#f2b33d) is never redefined for the light theme, in neither the prefers-color-scheme block nor [data-theme=light]. The 'beta' warning tag renders amber on #f2f4f8, a contrast ratio of 1.69:1, far below the 4.5:1 required. The one tag meant to stop admins using beta endpoints is the hardest one to read. REPRO: Use colorScheme 'light' (or the theme toggle), open http://localhost:4400/?c=graph:Get-MgBetaUser and compute contrast of .tags .tag-warn: color rgb(242,179,61) on bg rgb(242,244,248) = 1.69:1. Dark theme gives 9.26:1. The same amber text shows in the screenshot at 390x844.
DETL-05.E2 [ux/low] Extra values have no label. 'Primary', 'CAS', 'SMS Provider' and 'v1.0' sit alone among other tags, and nothing (no title, no prefix) says they are a site role or API version. 'Primary' in particular is ambiguous. REPRO: Open ?c=mecm:Add-CMBoundaryToGroup. The last tag reads 'Primary', with no title or 'Site role' context. Only the module version tag has a title.

User story: As an admin, I want to see how many permissions a cmdlet needs from the header so that I know whether there is a permissions section to review.

User story: As an admin, I want to copy the cmdlet name with one click so that I can paste it straight into my shell.

Errors found: DETL-08.E1 [logic/low] The 1400ms timers are never cleared. A second copy within 1.4s is reset by the first click's timer, so its 'Copied' confirmation shows for only about 0.4s. The same bug affects every copy button (Copy link, Copy code, Copy all permissions). REPRO: Open ?c=graph:Get-MgUser, click Copy name, wait 1000ms, click it again, wait 600ms. aria-label is already 'Copy name', though only 600ms have passed since the second copy (expected 'Copied' until 1400ms after it).

Feature: Loading skeleton while module file loads
User story: As an admin, I want a visible loading state while details are fetched so that I know the pane is working.
Expected behaviour: While the module file is being fetched, a div.detail-skel with aria-busy="true" and aria-label="Loading details" containing four shimmering span bars is shown under the header (header tags/links render immediately from the row).
How to test: Throttle network, open an uncached cmdlet; assert .detail-skel[aria-busy='true'] is present, then disappears when content loads.
Test result: Module fetches were delayed 2.5s with page.route. div.detail-skel[aria-busy=true][aria-label='Loading details'] has 4 spans with the shimmer 1.4s animation. Header tags (6) and both links render right away. The skeleton is visible in both themes (screenshots skel-dark.png / skel-light.png) and is removed once .detail-desc appears.
Errors found: DETL-10.E1 [accessibility/low] Under prefers-reduced-motion, the shimmer is not stopped. The global rule only shortens it to 0.01ms infinite, so the gradient keeps jumping between positions every frame instead of standing still. Separately, aria-label on a div with no role is ignored by most screen readers, so 'Loading details' is not announced. REPRO: Use reducedMotion 'reduce', delay /a/*/data/** by 6s, open ?c=graph:Get-MgUser, and screenshot a 400x4 strip of the 4th skeleton bar 8 times, 90ms apart. 5 distinct images result, so the bar is still moving.

User story: As an admin, I want a clear error if the details cannot be loaded so that I know to retry instead of seeing a blank pane.
Expected behaviour: If the module file fetch fails (non-2xx gives 'HTTP <status> for <path>'; network error) or the file has no record for the row's name (index and file from different deploys: 'no record for <name>'), a p.notice.notice-error role=alert reads 'Couldn’t load details (<message>). Check your connection and pick the cmdlet again.' A failed fetch is evicted from the module cache so reopening the cmdlet retries.
How to test: Block requests to /a/*/data/* (route abort), open a cmdlet; assert [role=alert].notice-error contains 'Couldn’t load details'. Unblock, open another row then the same one again; assert details render.
Test result: With route abort the page shows [role=alert].notice-error: 'Couldn’t load details (Failed to fetch). Check your connection and pick the cmdlet again.' A 404 gives 'HTTP 404 for data/az/Az.Compute.json'. '{}' gives 'no record for Get-AzVM'. Invalid JSON gives 'Unexpected token '<'...'. Contrast is good in both themes. After unblocking, opening another row and then Get-AzVM again makes a new request and the details render, so the cache eviction works. Two UX gaps, below.
Errors found:
DETL-11.E1 [ux/medium] 'Pick the cmdlet again' does not work when the admin does what it says. Clicking the same, still-open result row is a no-op: the Detail key does not change and nothing retries. The admin has to open a different cmdlet first and then come back. There is no Retry button. REPRO: Search 'Get-AzVM', route-abort /a/*/data/**, and click the first result (error shown). Remove the abort and click the same first result again. The alert stays and 0 new requests are made. Only clicking result 2 and then result 1 loads the details.
DETL-11.E2 [ux/low] The same advice, 'Check your connection', appears for failures that have nothing to do with the connection: 'no record for X' (index and file from different deploys) and invalid JSON. For a deploy mismatch the fix is to reload the page, and the raw JSON parser message is shown to the admin. REPRO: Fulfil /a/*/data/** with 200 '{}' or '<html>' and open ?c=az:Get-AzVM. The message is 'Couldn’t load details (no record for Get-AzVM). Check your connection…' or 'Couldn’t load details (Unexpected token '<', "<html>" is not valid JSON). Check your connection…'.

User story: As an admin, I want cmdlets from a module I've already opened to show instantly so that browsing related cmdlets is fast.
Expected behaviour: loadModule caches the fetch promise per source/file key; opening another cmdlet in the same module file reuses it with no new network request. Rejected promises are removed from the cache.
How to test: Open one cmdlet, then another in the same module (e.g. via the Same noun list); assert no second request to the same /a/<build>/data/<source>/<file> URL in the network log.
Test result: Playwright 1440x900: opened Get-MgUser (one request to /a/4296a71d9cdd/data/graph/Microsoft.Graph.Users.json), then clicked Same noun > Update-MgUser: no new data requests. Rejection: page.route aborted the first Microsoft.Graph.Groups.json fetch. Get-MgGroup showed the error, and opening New-MgGroup afterwards made a fresh request that succeeded, so the failed promise is evicted. Re-clicking the same failed result, or pressing Enter in the search box, made 0 requests and the error stayed.
Errors found: DETL-12.E1 [ux/medium] The load-failure notice says 'Check your connection and pick the cmdlet again.', but picking the same cmdlet again does nothing. openRow sets the same row.key, so neither Detail nor CmdletEntry remounts, and the effect keyed on [row.key] never re-runs. The page offers no retry button, so the only ways to recover are to open a different cmdlet first or reload the page. REPRO: Block the first request to **/data/graph/Microsoft.Graph.Groups.json (e.g. Playwright route abort, or go offline), search Get-MgGroup and click the result. The error notice appears. Restore the network and click the same Get-MgGroup result again. Observed: no request is made and the error stays. Expected: the entry retries the load (or a Retry button is shown).

User story: As an admin, I want the cmdlet's description shown first so that I can confirm it does what I need.
Expected behaviour: When the cmdlet has a description it is rendered as p.detail-desc above the syntax; nothing is rendered when empty.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with a synopsis; assert .detail-desc is present with non-empty text.
Test result: Get-MgUser, Get-AzVM and Get-CMDevice render p.detail-desc above Syntax. An empty-description case could not be reached in the UI: all 66 empty-description az cmdlets (e.g. Get-AzArizeAIOrganization) are missing from the index. Data scan of dist/a/*/data: 324 descriptions contain a literal backslash-n or backslash-r, and 1,100 end in '...' after being cut at 300 characters by the pipeline.
Errors found:
DETL-13.E1 [logic/medium] 324 descriptions show literal escape sequences in the detail pane. New-MgUser renders 'Create a new user.\rThe request body contains...' and Update-AzMLWorkspaceJob renders '...Job.\r\nFor update case...'. The pipelines do not unescape these sequences or turn them into line breaks. REPRO: Open http://localhost:4400/?c=graph%3ANew-MgUser and read .detail-desc. Observed text: 'Create a new user.\rThe request body…' (with a literal backslash and r). Expected: a line break, or the text joined with a space.
DETL-13.E2 [ux/low] The detail pane, meant to show the full description, gets the same 300-character text the list uses (MAX_DESCRIPTION_LEN=300 in the graph and entra pipelines). It is cut mid-word with '...' (Get-MgUser: '...do a GET operation for th...'), there is no 'more' affordance, and 1,100 cmdlets are affected. REPRO: Open ?c=graph%3AGet-MgUser. The .detail-desc text ends with 'do a GET operation for th...'.
DETL-13.E3 [obsolete-path/low] 66 az cmdlets (e.g. the Az.ArizeAI and Az.Astro cmdlets) are written to the module files the site serves but have no manifest row. They cannot be searched or deep-linked: ?c=az%3AGet-AzArizeAIOrganization never resolves, so the data ships but cannot be reached. These are also exactly the 66 entries with an empty description. REPRO: Search 'Get-AzArizeAIOrganization' and see 'No match'. Then run grep Get-AzArizeAIOrganization dist/a/*/data/az/Az.ArizeAI.json and find the entry in the served file. The name is absent from data/az/manifest.json.

Feature: Syntax parameter sets with highlighting and copy
User story: As an admin, I want each parameter set's syntax shown, highlighted and copyable so that I can see valid argument combinations and paste a template.
Expected behaviour: Syntax text is split into parameter sets on blank lines; each non-empty set renders as div.code.code-syntax with a pre/code body and a 'Copy code' small icon button that copies the set's groups joined with single spaces (whitespace normalised). Heading is 'Syntax', with ' · N parameter sets' note when there is more than one set. Each top-level group (e.g. '-Name <T>', '[-Opt <T>]', '[-Switch]') is a span.sg that does not wrap internally, so lines break only between parameters; a bare <Type> joins the preceding group; brackets/angles are respected including malformed '[-Status <StatusEnum]'. Tokens are highlighted as t-cmd, t-param, t-type, etc. The section is omitted when there is no syntax.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with multiple parameter sets (e.g. Get-MgUser); assert h3 text contains 'parameter sets' and count of .code-syntax equals N; assert .code-syntax .sg elements exist and first contains span.t-cmd; click its 'Copy code' button and assert clipboard is a single-spaced line starting with the cmdlet name.
Test result: Get-MgUser (the story's example) shows a single Syntax block with no 'parameter sets' note: the data holds only its first set. Data scan: 40,951 of 41,021 cmdlets have exactly 1 set. Only 3 have more (New-AzNatGateway: 2; New/Set-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy: 6), and all 3 are one set wrapped with blank lines. For New-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy the h3 reads 'Syntax · 6 parameter sets', and the Copy on block 2 gives '[-AllowCallQueueWelcomeGreetingChange <Boolean>] ...' without the cmdlet name. Grouping and highlighting work: .sg groups keep '[-Status <StatusEnum]' and '[-Name] <String>' intact, and the first .sg holds span.t-cmd. On Get-MgUser the copy produced a single-spaced line equal to the pre text. At 390px the syntax pre scrolls horizontally (scrollWidth 532 vs 356) with the right-edge fade.
Errors found:
DETL-14.E1 [logic/high] Every pipeline keeps only the first code block of SYNTAX (graph/entra extract_first_code_block, az/exchange extract_code_blocks(...,1)[0], mecm parse_syntax 'first syntax block', az get-azcmdlets.ps1 'first variant'). Real parameter sets are dropped. For Get-MgUser the List set is shown, and -UserId and -InputObject appear nowhere on the page, so an admin cannot learn how to fetch one user. The multi-set UI is effectively dead code for real data. REPRO: Open ?c=graph%3AGet-MgUser. Observed: 1 .code-syntax, the h3 is just 'Syntax', and the table has no -UserId row. Expected (per the story's test): several parameter sets, including the Get set with -UserId.
DETL-14.E2 [logic/medium] parseSyntax splits on any blank line, so a single set that the docs wrap with blank lines becomes N fake 'parameter sets'. Blocks 2..N have no cmdlet name and copy as fragments that cannot be pasted and run. New-AzNatGateway's second 'set' is just '[<CommonParameters>]'. REPRO: Open ?c=exchange%3ANew-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy. The h3 says 'Syntax · 6 parameter sets', and 6 .code-syntax blocks appear, only the first starting with New-CsTeamsVoiceApplicationsPolicy. Click Copy code on the 2nd block: the clipboard starts '[-AllowCallQueueWelcomeGreetingChange <Boolean>]'. Expected: 1 set. Also see ?c=az%3ANew-AzNatGateway.

User story: As an admin, I want a table of parameters with types and required/positional markers so that I know what I must supply.
Expected behaviour: Parameters parsed from all syntax sets are deduplicated by name, shown in table.params with columns Name (code.t-param '-Name' plus optional p.param-desc), Type (code.t-type; 'Switch' when no type), and a visually-hidden 'Required' column. A parameter is Required (span.tag.tag-req) only if every set requires it; otherwise a '[-Name] <T>' parameter shows a 'Positional' tag; otherwise empty. Required parameters are sorted first. If a name's first occurrence was a switch, a later typed occurrence supplies its type. The section is omitted when no visible parameters.
How to test: Open a cmdlet with a mandatory parameter (e.g. New-MgUser or Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName); assert table.params rows exist, rows with .tag-req appear before those without, and a switch parameter shows type 'Switch'.
Test result: New-UMAutoAttendant: -Name String Required and -UMDialPlan Required are listed first, and switches show 'Switch'. Get-AzVM: -ResourceGroupName and -Name show Positional, and -Status shows Switch. Malformed '[-Status <StatusEnum]' gives type StatusEnum. A unit check of parseSyntax with 'Get-X [-A <T>]\n\nGet-X -C <String>' returned C required:true even though set 1 does not contain C. At 390px the Type column breaks words mid-letter ('Strin|g', 'Switc|hParameter').
Errors found:
DETL-15.E1 [logic/low] 'Required only if every set requires it' is checked only across the sets where the parameter appears. A parameter that is mandatory in one set and absent from another is still tagged Required. This is latent today only because the pipelines drop extra sets (see DETL-14); once sets are restored it will mislabel e.g. -UserId on Get-MgUser. REPRO: node: parseSyntax('Get-X [-A <T>]\n\nGet-X -C <String>').params gives C {required:true}. Expected: required:false, since Get-X runs without -C in set 1.
DETL-15.E2 [ux/low] At phone width the Type column wraps type names at any character (overflow-wrap:anywhere), producing 'Strin/g' and 'IResu/ltObj/ect', which is hard to read. REPRO: Viewport 390x844, open ?c=mecm%3AGet-CMDevice and look at the Type column of table.params.

Feature: Hide pipeline/proxy common parameters behind a toggle
User story: As an admin, I want boilerplate pipeline and proxy parameters hidden by default so that the table shows the parameters that matter.
Expected behaviour: Parameters named Break, Headers, HttpPipelineAppend, HttpPipelinePrepend, Proxy, ProxyCredential, ProxyUseDefaultCredentials, ResponseHeadersVariable, WhatIf, Confirm, DefaultProfile are hidden initially and sorted last. A button.link-btn 'Show N pipeline and proxy parameters' (N = hidden count) appears when any are hidden; clicking it reveals them and the button disappears. State resets when a different entry opens.
How to test: Open a Graph cmdlet; assert no row with '-HttpPipelineAppend', click button.link-btn matching /Show \d+ pipeline and proxy parameters/, assert the row appears and the button is gone.

Area: navigation, URL state, sources and filters
Feature: Closing an entry removes it from the URL
User story: As an admin, I want closing the open cmdlet to clear it from the link so that the URL matches what I see.
Expected behaviour: Escape in the search box closes an open entry (or pending deep link) first; the c parameter is removed while q and filters stay. If nothing is open, Escape clears the query instead (removing q).
How to test: Load /?q=user&c=graph:Get-MgUser; focus input; press Escape; assert location.search === '?q=user'. Press Escape again; assert location.search === ''.
Test result: On /?q=user&c=graph:Get-MgUser, focusing the input and pressing Escape once left location.search empty: both c and q were removed. An event trace on the input showed ['input:', 'search'], meaning Chrome's native type=search Escape clears the value. A synthetic keydown Escape (no native default) gave ?q=user as specified. After clicking a result, focus is on BODY and Escape does nothing.
Errors found:
NAV-16.E1 [logic/high] The first Escape closes the entry and also clears the query. The input is type=search, and Chromium clears a search field on Escape and fires an input event. onKeyDown handles Escape but never calls preventDefault, so onQuery('') runs as well. The documented two-step 'close entry, then clear query' never happens in Chrome or Edge. REPRO: Load /?q=user&c=graph:Get-MgUser, wait for the detail, click into the search box and press Escape. Observed: location.search === '' and the input is empty. Expected: '?q=user' with the query kept. Fix: call e.preventDefault() in the Escape branch of onKeyDown.
NAV-16.E2 [accessibility/medium] On desktop the only keyboard or mouse way to close an open entry is Escape while focus is in the search box. Clicking a result moves focus to BODY, and Escape there (or inside the detail pane) does nothing. The back button is display:none above 900px, yet the intro hint advertises 'Esc close'. REPRO: At 1440x900 load /?q=user, click the second result, then press Escape. Observed: c stays in the URL and the detail stays open. Also click inside the detail title and press Escape: nothing happens. Expected: a global Escape closes the entry, or a visible close control.
NAV-16.E3 [accessibility/medium] The search box loses autofocus once the app mounts. The server Shell's input is focused, then Shell is replaced by Search and the new input is not focused, so document.activeElement becomes BODY. Text typed right after load goes nowhere, and Escape and arrow keys do nothing until the user clicks the box or presses '/'. REPRO: Load / and wait for .app[aria-busy] to go away. Observed: document.activeElement is BODY, and keyboard.type('mguser') leaves the input empty and the URL unchanged. Before mount activeElement was INPUT. Expected: the search input is focused after mount.

User story: As an admin, I want the page frame to appear immediately while the search session starts so that I see where to type before the index loads.
Expected behaviour: The SSR/first-paint render is <Shell/> (App returns Shell until a mount effect flips `mounted`). Shell renders Frame with inert=true, so the root .app div carries aria-busy="true"; the band shows the All tab selected, empty query, placeholder `Search <TOTAL> cmdlets`; the toolbar count reads "Loading index…" with a 0-count Filters chip; the results pane shows ResultsSkeleton shimmer rows and the detail pane shows the Intro. Test result: curl of the served page (identical to dist/index.html): .app aria-busy="true", .count 'Loading index…', 12 result-skel, .intro present, placeholder 'Search 40,931 cmdlets', All tab aria-pressed=true, Filters chip with no count. But Playwright (t1.cjs, t12.cjs) shows the SSR input is autofocused and editable before hydration, and Search then replaces Shell with a new DOM tree, so focus and any typed text are lost.
Errors found:
SHEL-01.E1 [ux/high] The search box is not focused after the page loads. The SSR input has autofocus, but App swaps <Shell/> for <Search/>, which are different component types. Preact unmounts the whole tree and creates a new <input>, and autofocus does not apply to elements inserted later. document.activeElement stays BODY, so an admin who loads the page and starts typing gets nothing. App.tsx's onKeyDown comment ('The box is autofocused') assumes otherwise. REPRO: Playwright 1440x900: goto http://localhost:4400, wait until .app has no aria-busy, then wait 0/300/1500 ms. document.activeElement.tagName is 'BODY' at every point. keyboard.type('abc') leaves the input value ''. After hydration the input value is '' and the URL is http://localhost:4400/. Expected: the typed query is kept, or the input is visibly disabled until ready.

User story: As a maintainer, I want the index build to refuse to run when the source lists disagree so that a source added or removed in one place cannot silently be missing from the site or the refresh workflow.
Expected behaviour: Before anything is written, checkRegistries() compares the sorted ids of SOURCES (graph, az, entra, exchange, mecm) with the sorted directory names under data/ and the directories under pipelines/ that contain a source.env. If either list differs, the build throws `Source lists disagree. SOURCES: <ids>; data/: <dirs>; pipelines/*/source.env: <dirs>` and exits 1 (main().catch -> process.exit(1)); public/a/ is not removed because the check runs before rm(OUT). Directories under pipelines/ without source.env (e.g. __pycache__) are ignored; plain files in data/ are ignored.
How to test: Copy the repo to a scratch dir; `mkdir data/foo && npm run index` -> exit code 1 and stderr contains 'Source lists disagree' and 'data/: az,entra,exchange,foo,graph,mecm'. Revert, then `mkdir pipelines/bar && touch pipelines/bar/source.env && npm run index` -> same error naming pipelines list. With a clean tree `npm run index` exits 0.
Test result: Scratch copy repo-bld: mkdir data/foo -> exit 1, 'Source lists disagree. SOURCES: az,entra,exchange,graph,mecm; data/: az,entra,exchange,foo,graph,mecm; ...', public/a/4296a71d9cdd kept. pipelines/bar/source.env -> same error naming 'pipelines/*/source.env: az,bar,...'. Removing data/mecm also caught. pipelines/__pycache__ and a plain file data/README ignored (exit 0). Clean tree exit 0. A hidden dir data/.cache also fails the build; a symlinked data dir is silently ignored.

User story: As a maintainer, I want a malformed data/<source>/manifest.json or descriptions.json to fail the build with a precise message so that a parser change that breaks the shape never ships a broken index.
Expected behaviour: loadRows throws (build exits 1) when: manifest is not an object (`<id> manifest: not an object`); descriptions.json is not an object of strings (`<id> descriptions: not an object of strings`); manifest.d is not an array (`<id> manifest: d is not a list`); manifest.v is missing, non-string or empty (`<id> manifest: v is not a version string`). Per row (parseManifestRow): non-object row; missing/non-string n (`n (name) is not a string`); non-string v or c (`<k> is not a string`); m missing for a source without a fixed module (all but mecm) or empty (`no module`); the row's name appears in no module file (`no module file`); the module matches none of the files holding the name (`module <m> matches none of its files (<files>)`); for sources with an extra facet (graph/entra field a, mecm field r) the field must be a string. Errors are prefixed `<id> manifest, <name>:`. For mecm, a row without m gets module 'ConfigurationManager' and resolves to the single file holding the name.
How to test: In a scratch copy, edit data/az/manifest.json: set "v":"" -> `npm run index` fails with 'az manifest: v is not a version string'. Restore; remove the 'm' key from one az row -> fails with 'az manifest, <name>: m is not a string'. Restore; change one graph row's m to 'Nope' -> 'module Nope matches none of its files'. Restore; delete a graph row's 'a' -> 'a is not a string'.
Test result: Mutation tests in the scratch copy all fail with the documented messages: v='' / missing / 5 -> 'az manifest: v is not a version string'; d={} -> 'd is not a list'; manifest [] or null -> 'not an object'; descriptions [] or non-string -> 'az descriptions: not an object of strings'; row without m -> 'az manifest, Get-AzADDomainService: m is not a string'; m='' -> 'no module'; unknown name -> 'no module file'; graph m=Nope -> 'module Nope matches none of its files (Microsoft.Graph.Applications)'; graph without a -> 'a is not a string'; mecm without r -> 'r is not a string'; mecm rows resolve to module ConfigurationManager. Gaps: duplicate rows, a wrong explicit m on mecm, and a non-boolean e are all accepted. Also a failed validation wipes public/a.
Errors found:
BLD-02.E1 [logic/medium] Duplicate manifest rows are not rejected. The same cmdlet goes into the shard twice, the source count and the site-wide total go up by one, and search shows the cmdlet twice. REPRO: Scratch copy: node mut.cjs data/az/manifest.json 'j.d.push(j.d[0])'; npm run index -> exit 0, '40932 cmdlets indexed' (was 40931). Expected: '<id> manifest, <name>: duplicate row' and exit 1.

The bogus module becomes the row's module and its Module facet value, because the single-file fallback runs whatever m says. REPRO: Scratch copy: set data/mecm/manifest.json d[0].m='Wrong'; npm run index -> exit 0. The idx/mecm.json mods table now contains 'Wrong'.
BLD-02.E3 [logic/low] A validation failure in loadRows happens after rm(OUT). The previous good public/a/<build> is gone and a partial public/a/.staging is left behind, while src/sources.generated.json still names the old build. A dev server that is already running then gets 404 for every artifact until a build succeeds. Expected: the previous build stays in place until the new one is complete.

Feature: Immutable caching of build artifacts on Vercel
User story: As a maintainer, I want hashed artifact URLs served with a long immutable cache so that repeat visitors never re-download unchanged index data.
Expected behaviour: vercel.json sets framework astro, buildCommand `npm run build` (which runs `npm run index` then `astro build`), outputDirectory dist, and a header rule for source /a/(.*) adding `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Other paths get no custom cache header.
How to test: `jq '.headers' vercel.json` shows the /a/(.*) rule. Against a deployment: `curl -sI https://<site>/a/<build>/idx/az.json | grep -i cache-control` -> 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'; `curl -sI https://<site>/` does not have that value.
Test result: vercel.json has framework astro, buildCommand 'npm run build' (which runs index, then astro build), outputDirectory dist, and one header rule: /a/(.*) -> 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. No other custom headers. Locally, astro preview sends 'Cache-Control: no-cache' for /a/ and / as expected, since the header is Vercel-only. A deployed site is unreachable from here, so the live header can't be verified.
